subject: Debrief: Backend Engineer candidate Ben Turner — collect scorecards & recommend
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@talentbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Debrief: Backend Engineer candidate Ben Turner — collect scorecards & recommend

Team —

Quick debrief ask for Ben Turner (applied for Backend Engineer). He finished his take-home + three interviews yesterday: system design with Marcus, infra/observability with Marissa, and coding pair with Tessa. Resume attached for reference (resume_bturner.pdf).

Please do two things by end-of-day tomorrow (Thu 2/16):
1) Drop your numeric score (1-5) on the shared scorecard and a 1-2 sentence rationale for any score <=3 or >=4.5. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-turner-feedback.
2) Flag any blocking concerns (culture/communication/skill gaps) explicitly — we need to either schedule a follow-up or close the loop.

I attached a blank scorecard template (turner_initial_scorecard_template.xlsx) — if you already exported a PDF/marked version, just attach here or upload to the Drive.

Callout: hiring bar we use is >=3.6 average AND no blocking concerns. If we land on 3.5–3.6 with no blocks and a clear plan for growth, can discuss as a manager-exception.

Thanks — I can synthesize afterward and recommend next step (onsite vs. pass).

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Staff Software Engineer, Backend Hiring Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: resume_bturner.pdf (PDF), turner_initial_scorecard_template.xlsx (XLSX)

Blocking? No.

Subject: Re: Debrief: Backend Engineer candidate Ben Turner — collect scorecards & recommend

Diego — thanks for organizing.

Score (1-5): 4.2
Notes: Ben gave a solid system-design answer for the token service: clear API surface, partitioning plan, and reasonable cache invalidation approach. I pushed him on failure modes (zookeeper style leader elections vs. centralized lease). He pivoted and suggested an acceptable fallback. My only hesitation is that his latency-first bias may underweight eventual consistency tradeoffs; worth calling out but not a blocker.

Marcus

Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Feb 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Debrief: Backend Engineer candidate Ben Turner — collect scorecards & recommend

Thanks all — quick update and my final read.

Score (1-5): 3.6
Notes: Pairing was okay; Ben solved the core problem but needed hints on edge-case inputs and thought-time on API ergonomics. No red flags on debugging skills; would need mentoring on code hygiene and testing patterns.

Monica also pinged me with a short voice — her summary: 3.4, concerns about consistency on design writeups.

Synthesis (Diego, feel free to revise):
- Scores collected: Marcus 4.2, Marissa 3.8, Tessa 3.6, Monica 3.4 => avg = 3.75
- Blocks: none explicit, but pattern: needs stronger consistency modeling and some CS fundamentals polish.
- Recommendation: Move to one final deep design callback (45m) focused on consistency / failure modes + a short coding rubric check; keep it lightweight. If that goes well, extend offer.

Action: Diego, if you’re aligned I’ll coordinate scheduling with Aisha/TalentBridge and share two proposed slots next week.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Principal SWE, Core Services
Redwood Inference
